propositions: A committed lock freezes transitive dependencies, causing any published advisory against a pinned version to block all in-flight changes regardless of whether those changes touch the dependency map

Unrelated changes incorrectly blocked by advisories should not fail Gerrit verify; only changes that touch the dependency map (uv.lock/pyproject.toml) are responsible for owning and resolving advisories in that lane

override-dependencies is the correct instrument to bypass an upstream cap; constraint-dependencies can only narrow existing constraints and returns UNSATISFIABLE as expected output, which does not prove an upgrade is impossible
pip-audit retry logic only rehecks DB-unreachable failures, so recheck cannot clear a real advisory finding and must be distinguished from transient failures in job output
A scheduled canary must escalate outstanding transitive-dependency advisories from main branch with dedup to avoid filing duplicate tickets, and block releases until the advisory is resolved
